introduction.text: The Fontana dei Libri is a fountain in Rome that marks the site of the Palazzo della Sapienza and is notable for its distinctive design featuring books and a deer, reflecting the local rione and the university.

history.description: The fountain was built by Pietro Lombardi between 1925 and 1927 as the last of ten fountains.
The fountain was restored in 1998 to remove limestone deposits.
The fountain was restored again in 2018 after damage to a nearby fountain.
The fasces symbols on the books were removed after the establishment of the republic.
The rione's number is engraved as IV instead of the correct VIII.

design.description: The fountain features a deer from the rione's coat of arms, two stacks of books symbolizing Sapienza University, and an engraved rione name and number.
The fountain replaced an iron nasone that was considered unsightly.
